comparison: Both strongly support claims C18-C25 regarding the requirement of MTA and MTB in the same cell. OpenEval emphasizes the pre-incubation experiments and argues against a simple receptor-ligand model. Peer reviewers accept the findings as 'unequivocal' and 'well-designed,' though Reviewer 1 separately challenges the dismissal of the receptor-ligand model (see R5/R7 pairing).

Major disagreement on self-recognition mechanism (C86-C92, C94, C98). OpenEval finds the inhibition experiments support self-recognition. Reviewer 3 explicitly challenges this interpretation, arguing the data could reflect competitive inhibition rather than active self-recognition, and states 'a claim of self-recognition through the MTA and MTB should not be made.'

Both support claims C30-C38 regarding differential requirements for costimulation markers. OpenEval describes the two-stage model as 'well-documented.' Peer reviewers accept the findings, with Reviewer 1 describing the assays as 'sophisticated and well-designed.' No challenges to the differential requirements or two-stage model.

Partial disagreement on non-self recognition mechanism (C78-C85, C92, C98). OpenEval finds the stimulation experiments with recombinant proteins strongly support non-self recognition. Reviewer 1 raises a critical concern about why extracellular fragments stimulate pairing but don't induce costimulation alone, questioning the mechanistic interpretation despite accepting the pairing rate effects.

Both support background claims C1-C9 about T. thermophila mating-type biology. OpenEval cites established literature. Peer reviewers accept these as established knowledge, though Reviewer 3 requests clearer presentation for a general audience. Also covers C10-C17 on genetic basis, which both sides accept from prior work.

Both support claims C108-C112 regarding the selfing phenotype of MTB2-eGFP strain. OpenEval finds the mating pattern and interpretation logical. Peer reviewers accept these observations without challenge, treating them as supporting evidence for broader mechanistic conclusions.

Both support MTRC component characterization (C49-C56). OpenEval finds bioinformatic analysis and genome sequencing well-documented. Peer reviewers accept the identification of the six-protein MRC complex as 'quite intriguing,' though Reviewer 2 suggests functional characterization of at least one MRC subunit would strengthen the findings. Also covers C42-C46, C57-C58, C60-C62 on complex identification.

Both strongly support localization findings (C63-C66). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple methods (fractionation, biotinylation, microscopy, MS). Peer reviewers accept the surface localization and absence from cilia without challenge, noting the 'varied set of protein isolation and characterization techniques.' Also covers C72-C76 on fluorescent tagging.

Both support fluorescent tagging localization (C67-C76). OpenEval finds functional validation and microscopy provide strong support. Peer reviewers accept the surface localization findings as part of the comprehensive localization evidence, with no challenges to the microscopy or MS data.

Disagreement on receptor-ligand model dismissal (C25-C27, C39-C42). OpenEval finds the MTRC hypothesis strongly supported by the contrast between mutant mixing and pre-incubation experiments. Reviewer 1 directly challenges this: 'The authors dismiss the possibility of a "simple receptor-ligand system", even though the data does not exclude this possibility,' arguing the data are compatible with MTA as ligand and MTB as receptor or vice-versa.

Both support IP-MS identification of MTRC (C43-C46). OpenEval emphasizes co-purification and use of multiple baits with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers accept the complex identification, with Reviewer 2 finding it 'quite intriguing,' though suggesting additional functional validation would strengthen the findings.

Both support identification of additional interacting proteins (C57-C58, C60-C62). OpenEval acknowledges weaker IP-MS evidence but notes converging support from coexpression and phenotypes. Peer reviewers accept these proteins as part of the MTRC characterization, with Reviewer 2 suggesting functional analysis of at least one subunit.

Both support main conclusions (C93-C98) about MTA/MTB complex distinguishing self from non-self. OpenEval finds convergence of multiple approaches supports the novel mechanism. Peer reviewers accept the requirement of both proteins (C95-C96) but challenge specific aspects of the self-recognition interpretation (see R12/R6 pairing).

Both support genetic basis claims C10-C15. OpenEval cites prior work and deletion phenotypes. Peer reviewers accept these as established from previous studies, with Reviewer 3 noting the intriguing requirement for both allelic genes.

Both support claims C16-C17 summarizing prior work on CDK19/CYC9/CIP1. OpenEval notes these provide important context for weak IP-MS interactions. Peer reviewers accept these as established background from previous studies.

OpenEval supports evolutionary context claims C99-C101 comparing to other systems and noting length variation among Tetrahymena species. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific evolutionary comparisons.

OpenEval rates speculative mechanistic models (C102-C107) as UNCERTAIN, noting Ca2+ hypothesis and signaling mechanisms lack direct experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these mechanistic speculations.
OpenEval supports comparative context claim C113 about Paramecium mating systems based on established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparative claim.
OpenEval supports general background claims C114-C117 on sexual systems across biology with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these broad background claims.

OpenEval supports claims C118-C123 on nuclear biology and mating-type determination in T. thermophila as well-established background. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims, though they are implicitly accepted.
